output.title: Aerobic Base Introduction
output.description: Process: Warm up 10 min easy walking and light jogging @ 6:30 /km → Continuous run 30 min @ Zone 2 (5:35 /km, HR 135-148 bpm) → Cool down 10 min easy jog and walking @ 6:40 /km. Overall: A steady introductory Zone 2 aerobic maintenance run on flat terrain to establish aerobic metabolism for the block. Keeps systemic fatigue negligible while stimulating mitochondrial density and capillary growth. Sets a solid baseline for the upcoming muscular endurance and long run volume. Reason: Scheduled on the opening day of the plan to kickstart aerobic continuity without accumulating central nervous system fatigue. Benefit: Enhances cardiac stroke volume, slow-twitch muscle fiber oxidative capacity, and fatty acid oxidation efficiency. Warning: Do not exceed Zone 2 heart rate ceiling (150 bpm); reduce pace promptly if cardiovascular drift begins.
output.fueling_tip: Plain water and optional electrolytes (200-400mg sodium) as duration is under 75 minutes; no exogenous carbohydrates required.

output.title: Bodyweight Muscular Endurance Circuit
output.description: Process: Warm up 10 min dynamic mobility and joint preparation → 10 reps Split Jump Squats, 15s transition → 10 reps Squat Jumps, 15s transition → 10 reps/leg Box Step-Ups at 75% kneecap height, 15s transition → 10 reps/leg Front Lunges → Rest 60s between rounds for 6 total rounds (25 min total) → Cool down 10 min easy walking and lower body mobility. Overall: High-repetition, low-resistance bodyweight muscular endurance circuit designed specifically to condition propelling leg musculature without gym equipment. Induces a strong peripheral burn in the quadriceps and glutes while keeping cardiovascular strain strictly within aerobic limits. Compensates for flat training terrain by building fatigue-resistant frontier muscle fibers for trail climbing. Reason: Scheduled on Thursday to place high-force chassis conditioning early in the microcycle, maintaining the mandatory 48-hour separation before Sunday's long run. Benefit: Trains high-threshold FTa motor units to clear local lactate and sustain force output during sustained climbs and downhill braking. Warning: Terminate sets if movement mechanics deteriorate or knee valgus occurs; keep cardiovascular exertion strictly low while absorbing the muscular burn.
output.fueling_tip: Hydrate with 400-500ml water containing 200-400mg sodium during and after the circuit; no supplemental carbohydrates needed.

output.title: Aerobic Recovery & Flat Neuromuscular Strides
output.description: Process: Warm up 10 min easy jog @ 6:50 /km → Continuous run 25 min @ Zone 1-2 (6:25 /km, HR 125-138 bpm) → 5 x 20s flat relaxed neuromuscular strides @ 3:55 /km with 40s easy walking recovery → Cool down 5 min walking @ 7:15 /km. Overall: A gentle aerobic flush to facilitate active recovery following Thursday's muscular endurance work while reinforcing stride mechanics. Flat accelerations recruit fast-twitch fibers without metabolic acidosis or systemic fatigue. Prepares the musculoskeletal system for weekend aerobic volume. Reason: Bridges the gap between high-force circuit training and the upcoming weekend run, preventing muscle stiffness and encouraging capillary blood flow. Benefit: Accelerates cellular clearance of metabolic byproducts, improves neuromuscular coordination, and preserves running economy. Warning: Ensure flat strides are fast and fluid with tall posture rather than all-out straining sprints; shut down immediately if any hamstring tightness arises.
output.fueling_tip: Drink 300-500ml water with light electrolytes (200-400mg sodium); exogenous carbs are unnecessary for this short, low-stress run.

output.title: Scheduled Rest & Regeneration
output.description: Process: Complete rest day with light mobility, tissue hydration, and full systemic regeneration. Overall: Complete day off from structured training to allow muscular and neural adaptation from the first half of the microcycle. Ensures muscle glycogen stores are fully replenished prior to Sunday's primary endurance session. Optimizes parasympathetic tone and connective tissue health. Reason: Scheduled to provide a dedicated 48-hour recovery cushion following Thursday's muscular endurance circuit and ensure freshness for the long run. Benefit: Restores neuromuscular excitability, consolidates structural adaptations, and mitigates injury risk. Warning: Avoid strenuous cross-training, excessive yard work, or prolonged standing that could compromise recovery.
output.fueling_tip: Focus on nutrient-dense whole foods, balanced hydration (2-2.5L water), and baseline electrolyte intake throughout the day.

output.title: Aerobic Long Run
output.description: Process: Warm up 10 min easy jog @ 6:20 /km → Continuous steady endurance run 60 min @ Zone 2 (5:35 /km, HR 135-148 bpm) → Cool down 10 min easy jog and walking @ 6:30 /km. Overall: The cornerstone endurance session of the week, maintaining strict Zone 2 intensity across flat terrain to build systemic fatigue resistance. Respects the 33% weekly volume cap while promoting mitochondrial density and fatty acid oxidation. Builds mental focus and musculoskeletal durability for trail race endurance. Reason: Placed at the end of the week to maximize weekly aerobic accumulation without compromising the following week's schedule. Benefit: Expands slow-twitch muscle fiber volume, enhances glycogen sparing at aerobic paces, and strengthens connective tissue. Warning: Strictly enforce the aerobic ceiling (AeT 150 bpm); walk or drop pace immediately if cardiac drift drives heart rate above threshold.
output.fueling_tip: Consume 30-40g carbohydrates per hour using energy chews or gels, paired with 400-600ml water and 300-500mg sodium per hour.
